context: Collapsible horizontal tree of biological taxonomy (~200 nodes, 6 ranks: Domain through Family) with text search, auto-expand to matches, rank-color legend, and descendant counts on collapsed nodes.
first_impression: Clean and well-managed — progressive disclosure keeps the default view to ~14 nodes and the rank-color palette is restrained and purposeful.
what_works: Descendant count badges (+37, +16, etc.) on collapsed nodes give spatial awareness of hidden depth without opening everything; the 6-color Tol palette maps cleanly to rank levels and the legend is immediately readable. Search auto-expands paths to matches, which collapses the interaction to one conceptual task at a time.
what_doesnt: All collapsed phylum nodes render as the same pink dot, making sibling phyla visually indistinguishable at a glance — rank color encodes level, not identity, so users must read labels rather than use color to differentiate peers. Animation congruence (transitions during expand/collapse and search) cannot be assessed from a static screenshot, and reheat behavior on large subtree expansions could produce disorienting motion.
